skill.name: azure-resource-visualizer
skill.description: Analyze Azure resource groups and create Mermaid architecture diagrams that show resources, configuration details, and relationships.
skill.summary: Create read-only Azure resource group architecture diagrams in Markdown and Mermaid.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, Mermaid diagram syntax, sample private IP ranges, and read-only Azure CLI examples. I found no prompt injection, covert data exfiltration, destructive Azure operation, or hidden executable payload in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Azure CLI fallback is broad compared with the read-only skill scope.
remediation.suggestion: State that all Azure CLI and MCP operations must be read-only, and require user confirmation before running inventory commands.

remediation.issue: Generated architecture documents can expose sensitive infrastructure topology.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to review diagrams before sharing them and to omit secrets, private endpoint details, and unnecessary identifiers.

content.value_statement: Azure resource groups can be hard to understand from inventory lists alone. This skill turns resource details into clear Mermaid diagrams and Markdown documentation.
actual_capabilities: Lists or validates Azure resource groups before analysis.
Discovers resources through Azure MCP tools, Azure CLI, or Resource Graph guidance.
Maps relationships between compute, network, data, security, and monitoring resources.
Creates Mermaid diagrams with grouped layers and labeled connections.
Generates Markdown architecture documentation from a provided template.
Handles large or complex resource groups by suggesting layered diagrams.
limitations: Requires Azure access through MCP tools or Azure CLI credentials.
Does not create, update, or delete Azure resources.
Diagram accuracy depends on available permissions and returned resource metadata.
Complex cross-subscription dependencies may need manual verification.

use_cases.title: Document a production resource group
use_cases.description: Create a clear architecture file that shows resources, tiers, regions, and connections for operational review.

use_cases.title: Prepare architecture handoff material
use_cases.description: Turn Azure inventory into a diagram and relationship notes for onboarding, incident response, or migration planning.

use_cases.title: Review resource relationships before changes
use_cases.description: Map network, identity, data, and dependency paths before planning infrastructure updates.

prompt_templates.title: Diagram one resource group
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known resource group.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Azure architecture diagram for resource group <name>. Include a resource inventory, relationship notes, and a Mermaid diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Choose from available groups
prompt_templates.scenario: User does not know the exact resource group name.
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Azure resource groups, ask me to choose one, then create a Mermaid architecture diagram for the selected group.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on network and identity
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of important architecture paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze resource group <name> and emphasize virtual networks, subnets, private endpoints, managed identities, Key Vault access, and data flows.

prompt_templates.title: Create layered documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced documentation for a large environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze resource group <name>. If it has many resources, create separate Mermaid diagrams for network, compute, data, security, and monitoring layers.

output_examples.input: Create an architecture diagram for resource group payments-prod.
output_examples.output: A Markdown architecture document with a resource inventory, a grouped Mermaid diagram, and relationship notes for the payments production resources.

output_examples.input: Show how the app, database, storage account, and Key Vault connect.
output_examples.output: A focused diagram and explanation that labels application traffic, database access, storage access, and managed identity paths.

output_examples.input: Document a large resource group by service layer.
output_examples.output: Separate architecture sections for network, compute, data, security, and monitoring, with notes about cross-layer dependencies.

best_practices: Confirm the target resource group before collecting inventory.
Use read-only Azure permissions when generating diagrams.
Review generated diagrams before sharing infrastructure details.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to modify or deploy Azure resources.
Do not publish diagrams that expose secrets or sensitive endpoints.
Do not assume relationships that are missing from Azure metadata.

faq.question: Does this skill change Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only analysis and documentation.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs Azure MCP tools or Azure CLI access with permission to read resource metadata.

faq.question: What format does it create?
faq.answer: It creates Markdown documentation with embedded Mermaid architecture diagrams.

faq.question: Can it handle large resource groups?
faq.answer: Yes. For complex groups, it can split diagrams by layer or resource purpose.

faq.question: Can it show cross-resource-group dependencies?
faq.answer: It can note external dependencies when metadata reveals them, but complex dependencies may need manual confirmation.

faq.question: Is the output safe to share publicly?
faq.answer: Review it first. Architecture diagrams can reveal sensitive topology, names, and access paths.
